output.title: Spot proof-of-concept debt before you call the pilot done
output.body:
If you run a small business, proof-of-concept debt is the work you quietly defer during a pilot: missing notes, an untested edge case, a brittle manual step, or a bug you tell yourself can wait. The mistake is not the deferred item. It is failing to decide whether it still belongs in pilot scope or has become something you now need to carry into a real workflow.

Use one simple checkpoint at the end of the pilot. Ask: is this still just a proof, or is this now the thing I must extend? If it is only a proof, keep the deferred items in a separate post-pilot list. If it is becoming a production candidate, pause expansion until the list is reviewed and priced as proper scope. Human approval stays with you.

The practical next step is a one-page record before sign-off: what was deferred, why it was deferred, and whether each item is essential before rollout or can wait until after launch. Review that page with the owner before you call the pilot complete. It is not a legal warranty; it is a working decision record so the “finished” pilot does not smuggle unfinished work into the next phase.
